parameters.content:
# Create and publish Shopify product videos with Zvid

Turn active Shopify apparel products into branded vertical videos, review them, and optionally attach the finished MP4s to the matching product pages. It is designed for ecommerce and marketing teams that want catalog-scale product creative without rebuilding every video by hand.

### How it works
The workflow reads active products, skips items already tagged or carrying usable video, maps product images and data into one shared Zvid design, validates the batch, and offers a free dry-run preview. Approved batches render together. Publishing uses Shopify's staged-upload flow, associates each hosted video with its product, and adds the processed tag only after Shopify accepts the request.

### Setup
1. Complete the Shopify and Zvid credential notes to the right.
2. Open Config and replace the store, brand, copy, palette, limits, and schedule values.
3. Keep `dryRun` true for the first manual execution.
4. Review the editor link and credit quote before rendering.
5. Keep `publishToShopify` false until the videos are approved.

### Customization
The sample is optimized for apparel with square studio or flat-lay images, description bullets, prices, and sizes. Other product categories can reuse the flow after changing the scene labels and copy in Config. Never put secrets in Config.

## Shopify app (2026+)

Shopify Admin → Settings → Apps → Develop apps → Build apps in Dev Dashboard. Create an app/version, request `read_products`, `write_products`, and `write_files`, release it, then install it on the target store.

## Get the Shopify token

Dev Dashboard apps show Client ID and Client secret—not a token. Exchange them with `POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token` using `grant_type=client_credentials`. Copy the returned `access_token`; it expires after 24 hours. The ID or secret alone is never the access token.

## Connect Shopify in n8n

Create Header Auth: Name `X-Shopify-Access-Token`; Value = returned Admin API token. Assign it to Get catalog, Create upload targets, Attach video, and Mark processed. Existing admin-created apps can use their installed token. Refresh expiring tokens before scheduled runs.

## Connect Zvid in n8n

Create a key at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys. Create Header Auth with Name `x-api-key` and Value `zvid_…`. Assign it to Validate project, Save draft, Submit bulk render, and Get batch status. Never paste either provider's secret into Config.

## Example catalog

Five unisex tees: Alpine Crest ivory ($34), Clay Pocket terracotta ($35), Dawnline washed black ($32), Harbor Stripe navy/ivory ($36), and Meadow Sprig sage ($30). Each has square studio or flat-lay imagery, product copy, and S–XXL variants.

## Product data used

Required: active title, public product image, and priced variant. Up to four images feed the scenes. Description bullets, sizes, vendor, type, prices, title, tags, handle, and storefront domain personalize the output. Missing essentials are reported in `skipped`.

## Safe run modes

Start with `dryRun: true` for free validation, quote, and editor link. Next use `dryRun: false` with `publishToShopify: false` for review links. Enable publishing only after approval: rendering consumes Zvid credits and publishing changes Shopify media.

## Why HTTP Request?

n8n's Shopify node does not expose the required GraphQL media selection, `stagedUploadsCreate`, signed multipart upload, `productUpdate(media: VIDEO)`, or `tagsAdd`. HTTP Request nodes keep the exact Shopify contract while credentials remain in n8n.

## Shopify video publishing

A public MP4 cannot be attached directly as hosted video. This flow reads file size, creates a staged target, uploads the MP4, then associates Shopify's staged URL. Only accepted products are tagged; Shopify processes the media asynchronously.

## Queue and final status

Successful products receive `zvid-video`; the query excludes that tag. Existing non-failed videos are skipped, so scheduled batches advance safely. Final media status is initially `PROCESSING`; confirm `READY` in Shopify Admin before treating it as live.

## 1. Start and load products

Manual test or daily schedule → Config → Shopify catalog → eligibility checks.

## 2. Build and validate

Create the shared video design, validate every product, then choose dry run or rendering.

## 3. Preview or render

Save a free editor draft, or submit and monitor one Zvid bulk render.

## 4. Review or publish

Map completed videos to Shopify product GIDs and stop for review unless publishing is enabled.

## 5. Stage videos in Shopify

Inspect each MP4, create secure upload targets, download, upload, and verify every staged transfer.

## 6. Attach, tag, summarize

Associate staged videos, tag only successful products, and return processing status plus failures.
